about_p1.en: Josephine is a AI policy researcher, bridgemaker, political organiser and strategist based in Berlin. Her work focuses on systemic analysis and political strategy with a focus on Geopolitics & Technology Governance (China & EU). Her work has bridged across civil society, industry and institutions to center critical risks of technology to the forefront of political design. With industry experience in Machine Learning, and visiting researcher to the United Nations Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty Conference (UN NPTC) she specialises in multilateral and systemic framing of technology and it's impacts.

title.en: Ontological Insecurity: Soverignty, Nationalism and how the EU navigates the China-US Competition for Market Dominance Artificial Inteliigence

body.en: This Working Paper provides an analysis of how the emergence of soverignty narrative around technological infrastructure and AI is a symptom of geopolitical insecurity as market forces are concentrated in the China-US bind. Consequently, as nationalism and defense heightens across European countries, the soverignty arguement leverages this approach as it races to find security. From this lens, taking on theories and frameworks from social movement strategies, the paper provides pointers for how institutions and movements can prepare capabilties and infrastructure for protecting public interest.
